Use this class-level skill when full-width and/or full-height solid lines partition a grid into rectangular regions and the expected output appears to summarize those panels. 2. **Infer panel-to-output mapping.** Test whether output dimensions equal the count of panel bands. Look for a panel-wise summary: binary occupancy, marker count, color count, density category, or a relation across corresponding panel positions. Avoid assuming a pixelwise overlay; panels may each collapse to a single output cell.
3. **Infer color roles from evidence.** Separate divider colors from panel colors. Identify candidate background and signal/marker colors from repeated structure and output, not simply raw global frequency. A sparse color may be foreground even when another panel has unusual frequencies.

5. **Implement a generic transform.** Derive separator positions, panel bounds, palette roles, and output shape from the input. Do not hardcode demo dimensions or specific locations. 6. **Verify whole grids.** Run the saved task transform on every received input-output pair and compare full dimensions and cells before submitting. Then produce the test answer by calling that exact transform. After verdict, preserve the verified task module as required by the benchmark.
